clue.text: Quickly write section on swimming stroke

parts.note: the crawl is the front stroke in swimming

explanation.surface: A note-taker dashes off a passage about freestyle swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to scribble hastily and untidily, which is how you write when in a hurry.

clue.text: Time to suppress belief and sadness

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a day is a period of time
an ism is a doctrine or belief

explanation.surface: A period in which faith is crushed, leaving gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like a call for T; here it is a whole period, the day, which 'to suppress' holds down around the belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a sinking feeling of distress and disappointment, close kin to sadness.

clue.text: Encourage moderate Tory about heroin

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the other here

parts.note: in British politics a wet is a moderate Conservative, a term from the Thatcher years
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Urging a centrist Conservative on a drugs matter.
explanation.walkthrough: A WET is a moderate member of Britain's Conservative (Tory) party, Thatcher's word for her softer colleagues; 'about' wraps it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet an appetite or interest is to sharpen and stimulate it, so to encourage it.

clue.text: Email rude comments on sergeant's dancing

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to flame someone is to send them abusive messages online
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: Online abuse aimed at a sergeant's moves on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Spanish style of dancing, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Search disposing of Queen's concern

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to ferret is to search about busily
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A hunt that rids itself of the monarch's worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' takes ER out of FERRET.
explanation.definitionFit: A fret is a state of worry, so a concern; to be in a fret is to be anxious.

clue.text: Love following the example of US singer/actor?

parts.note: Cher is the American singer and actress
the suffix -ish means in the manner of, like

explanation.surface: Adoring someone by copying an American star.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds a mock adjective, Cher-ish, meaning behaving like Cher.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to hold them dear, a verb sense of love.

clue.text: More black wool tangled in space

indicators.note: tangled means twisted into a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Extra dark yarn knotted up in a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' scrambles MORE, B and WOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move freely, room to stretch one's arms.

clue.text: Sash worn, mostly decorated

parts.note: a worn tyre or carpet is bald, threadbare

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: rich can mean ornate, lavishly decorated

explanation.surface: A sash is put on, largely ornamented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of RICH to leave RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt or band worn over one shoulder to carry a sword, a kind of sash.

clue.text: Adventure novel unexpectedly about geese, nothing less

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so the letters turn up out of order
less means minus, so one letter is taken from the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A thriller with a surprising plot about geese, with nothing missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O away from ABOUTGEESE and rearrange the rest; 'unexpectedly' is the anagram signal and 'less' the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Geste is P C Wren's 1924 Foreign Legion tale, a classic adventure story.

clue.text: Distinctive stamp long observed in court

indicators.note: seen inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A seal of approval yearned for and witnessed by a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb here, to yearn, not an adjective; 'observed in' means seen inside the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachet is a seal or mark, and by extension a stamp of prestige or distinction.

clue.text: Recording almost entirely worthless

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone
bum as an adjective means of poor quality, worthless

explanation.surface: A record that's close to being utterly rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' applies only to 'entirely'; 'worthless' is the informal adjective bum, as in a bum deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a collection of tracks issued together, a recording.

clue.text: Starts to turn ravaging, without intervention dropping to upsetting

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters
dropping means letting fall, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: automatic means working by itself, with no human intervention
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rampaging spin that runs itself, then descends into distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without intervention' is one phrase defining a self-running machine; 'dropping' takes the clue's 'to' out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traumatic causes deep emotional shock, so it is extremely distressing.

clue.text: Subordinate not quickly losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word sheds its first letter

parts.note: slowly means not quickly

explanation.surface: A junior who works at a snail's pace and is losing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the S from SLOWLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowly means low in rank or status, so inferior in position, as a subordinate is.

clue.text: Orange pip blown about in St Paul's Tube?

indicators.note: blown about means scattered by the wind, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fruit seed drifts on the air inside the cathedral or the Underground station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St Paul's' suggests the London Tube station; it is the cathedral, whose organ has pipes, here called tubes.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ pipe is one of the tubes through which air sounds in a church organ like St Paul's.

clue.text: Possession? Last of men in his power at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Men under a captain's control on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges N (the last of men) with HIS and POWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of having something as one's own, so possession.

clue.text: What this is until it isn't?

definitions.text: What this is until it isn't?

parts.words: What this is until it isn't?
parts.note: the clue refers to itself: a puzzle seems impossible to solve right up until the moment it is solved

explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is the clue itself, beyond solving until a solver cracks it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insoluble means impossible to solve, which describes any puzzle before its answer is found.

clue.text: Seal fate: explorer soon goes travelling east

parts.note: Captain James Cook was the British explorer of the Pacific

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A navigator is soon to set off eastward and seal his fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges SOON GOES into ONES GOOS, between COOK and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook one's goose is an idiom for ruining one's own chances, so sealing one's fate.

clue.text: Flying kites filled with writing material — most abnormal

indicators.note: filled with means having something put inside, so one piece encloses the other
flying means moving through the air at random, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ink is what pens write with

explanation.surface: Kites soaring, stuffed with stationery: very odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' scrambles the kites into KIEST before 'filled with' adds the writing material.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkiest means most weird or deviant, the superlative of kinky, so most abnormal.

clue.text: Bishop half-throttled by his superior? That's right

indicators.note: only half of the bishop is gripped by the throat of his superior, so one of its letters is moved inside

parts.note: a bishop's ultimate superior is the Pope
RR, Right Reverend, is the style of a bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric partly strangled by his boss, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is Right Reverend; 'half-throttled by' means only one of his two letters ends up inside the superior's name, the other left trailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or fitting, so that's right.

clue.text: Borrow book? French novel you once observed to be about railway

parts.note: roman is the French word for novel

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Lending out a book, a French novel set on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' is not lending but George Borrow, the Victorian writer of The Romany Rye; 'observed' is a link and 'about' wraps the old you round the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany Rye is an 1857 book by George Borrow, sequel to Lavengro.

clue.text: Old man restraining people heading off for a dance

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: pa, like old man, is slang for father

indicators.note: heading off means losing the head, the first letter

parts.note: folk are people

explanation.surface: A father holds back the crowd as they leave for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' beheads the people, and 'restraining' has the old man hold what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Opening place to go for pop festivals? Loves to get away

indicators.note: to get away means to escape, so these letters leave

parts.words: place to go for pop festivals
parts.note: a Portaloo is the British brand of portable toilet seen at festivals; to go is to relieve oneself
love in tennis scoring is nil, so each love is an O

explanation.surface: A gateway for concertgoers, with two lovers escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: A Portaloo is a British portable toilet; 'to get away' removes the two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a doorway or gateway, an opening to pass through.

clue.text: Queen avoiding area linked to unknown highway

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a quarter is a district or area of a city
in algebra, y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A monarch steers clear of a district, joining an uncharted road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes QU from QUARTER to leave ARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a main road, a major traffic route, by analogy with a blood vessel.

clue.text: Bar quiet during story by Republican newsman

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a story is a lie
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: In a pub, hushed through a tale told by a Republican reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' is a fib here, and 'during' puts the call for quiet within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper publisher is a man in the news business, a press baron.

clue.text: Attractive gesture current in the North

definitions.meaning: a beckoning signal, drawing someone towards you

explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' means drawing towards, not pretty: to beckon. A beck in northern England is a brook, a flowing current.
explanation.definitionFit: Beck means both a beckoning nod and a northern English brook.

clue.text: Ransack, tossing lire all over the place

indicators.note: tossing means throwing out, so this letter goes

parts.note: to rifle is to search through and ransack
L is the abbreviation for the Italian lira, plural lire

explanation.surface: A burglar ransacks a place, scattering Italian banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' removes L from RIFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rife means widespread, found everywhere, so all over the place.

clue.text: Ostensibly the Mechanical Turk's Rook also retracted, pinning Bishop

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook

indicators.note: pinning means holding down, gripping, so one piece holds the other inside
retracted means drawn back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: too means also
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Chess moves of the famous fake automaton: rook withdrawn, bishop pinned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracted' turns TOO into OOT and 'pinning' grips B inside it. The Mechanical Turk was an 18th-century chess automaton with a man hidden inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turk was presented as a chess-playing machine, so it was ostensibly a robot.

clue.text: Appears, needing drink after shock

indicators.note: after means the drink comes behind the shock

parts.note: to rock is to shock or stun
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone turns up wanting a stiff drink after a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock up is informal British for to arrive, to turn up casually.

clue.text: Tart on side of Parisian street recalled French idler

parts.note: a flan is an open tart

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A pastry beside a Paris street brings to mind a lazy Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals a French word for street; 'recalled' turns it round, and 'on side of' just sets the tart beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaneur is a stroller, a man about town who idles in the streets, a French word.
